title: Accel-NASBench: Sustainable Benchmarking for Accelerator-Aware NAS
problem: Neural Architecture Search requires extensive computational resources and relies on benchmarks using synthetic datasets with simplified assumptions. Existing NAS benchmarks produce unrealistic evaluations due to oversimplified dataset and model characteristics.
motivation: Enabling zero-cost hardware-aware NAS benchmarking is essential for democratizing neural architecture search across diverse accelerator platforms without prohibitive computational overhead.
method: The approach searches for learned shortcuts—fast approximations that replace full model training—which drastically reduce benchmark construction costs. It builds a benchmark that optimizes two goals simultaneously: achieving high accuracy on ImageNet2012 and running efficiently on actual hardware accelerators (GPUs, TPUs, and FPGAs). Unlike prior benchmarks using simplified synthetic data, this works with large-scale realistic datasets. The approach is validated through experiments with multiple neural architecture search algorithms (automated methods for finding good network designs).
key_novelty: First to create fast benchmarks for finding efficient neural networks on real hardware (GPUs, TPUs, FPGAs) by using shortcuts learned from data instead of simplified, synthetic datasets.
contributions: Technique for searching training proxies to dramatically reduce NAS benchmark construction costs
Open-source bi-objective NAS benchmark for ImageNet2012 combined with accelerator on-device performance
Demonstrated zero-cost capability to find state-of-the-art hardware-aware models
Multi-platform support enabling NAS across GPUs, TPUs, and FPGAs

metrics.accuracy: benchmark fidelity to ground truth hardware performance
metrics.speedup: computational cost reduction enabling zero-cost evaluation

limitations: Evaluation limited to ImageNet2012 dataset; generalization to other datasets and workloads is not discussed.
